relations.subject: Henry Steel Olcott
relations.evidence: In 1875, during a period of Buddhist revival, Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott had founded the Theosophical Society in New York City.

relations.subject: Helena Blavatsky
relations.evidence: In 1875, during a period of Buddhist revival, Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott had founded the Theosophical Society in New York City.

relations.subject: Anagarika Dharmapala
relations.evidence: The young Dharmapala helped Colonel Olcott in his work, particularly by acting as his translator.

relations.subject: Anagarika Dharmapala
relations.evidence: Dharmapala also became quite close to Madame Blavatsky, who advised him to study Pāli and to work for the good of humanity – which is what he did.

relations.subject: Anagarika Dharmapala
relations.evidence: The Maha Bodhi Society at Colombo was founded in 1891 but its offices were soon moved to Calcutta the following year in 1892.

relations.subject: Anagarika Dharmapala
relations.evidence: He attended Christian College, Kotte; St Benedict's College, Kotahena; S. Thomas' College, Mutwal and the Colombo Academy (Royal College).
